text: @rcall converts argument using from_sexp() converts return value using to_sexp(). built-conversions : NA error wherever value expected. Likewise, Int64 argument must whole number. Julia’s Int64 values become R doubles R’s standard integers 32 bits; return Int32 need R integer. binding package can support additional types defining methods JLBind.from_sexp(::Type{T}, x::SEXP) JLBind.to_sexp(x::T). JLBind also provides helpers building R objects directly, JLBind.data_frame(). See JLBind source existing conversions helpers. Sometimes object easier keep Julia convert R data structure. can pass objects reference using RRef{T}. R receives external pointer Julia object, allowing reused across calls. object released R garbage-collects reference. example, define mutable Julia object expose functions operate : R, can create counter update across calls: r_class() sets R class external pointer, package can define methods print() . argument declared RRef{Counter} also checks reference points Counter, rather accepting arbitrary Julia object.
code: mutable struct Counter     n::Int64 end  JLBind.r_class(::Type{Counter}) = "counter"  new_counter(start::Int64) = Counter(start) increment(c::Counter, by::Int64) = (c.n += by; c.n)  @rcall new_counter(start::Int64)::RRef{Counter} @rcall increment(c::RRef{Counter}, by::Int64)::Int64 counter <- new_counter(0) class(counter) #> [1] "counter"  increment(counter, 2) #> [1] 2

height::Float64 end struct Triangle <: Shape     base::Float64     height::Float64 end  JLBind.r_class(::Type{<:Shape}) = "shape"  area(s::Circle) = pi * s.radius^2 area(s::Square) = s.side^2 shape")) end  circle(radius::Float64) = Circle(radius) square(side::Float64) = Square(side) rectangle(width::Float64, height::Float64) = Rectangle(width, height) triangle(base::Float64, height::Float64) = Triangle(base, height) shape_area(@nospecialize(s::Shape)) = with_shape(area, s) scaled_area(@nospecialize(s::Shape), factor::Float64) =     with_shape(x -> factor^2 * area(x), s)  @rcall circle(radius::Float64)::RRef{Shape} @rcall square(side::Float64)::RRef{Shape} @rcall rectangle(width::Float64, height::Float64)::RRef{Shape} @rcall triangle(base::Float64, height::Float64)::RRef{Shape} @rcall shape_area(s::RRef{Shape})::Float64 @rcall scaled_area(s::RRef{Shape}, factor::Float64)::Float64 circle <- function(radius) .Call(C_circle, radius) square <- function(side) .Call(C_square, side) rectangle <- function(width, height) .Call(C_rectangle, width, height) triangle <- function(base, height) .Call(C_triangle, base, height) shape_area <- function(shape) .Call(C_shape_area, shape) scaled_area <- function(shape, factor) .Call(C_scaled_area, shape, factor) shapes <- list(circle(1), square(2), rectangle(2, 3), triangle(2, 3)) vapply(shapes, shape_area, numeric(1)) #> [1] 3.141593 4.000000 6.000000 3.000000  scaled_area(square(2), 3) #> [1] 36

title: Update the list of Julia functions R can call — update_entrypoints
code: # A package set up with use_jlbind() in a temporary directory pkg <- file.path(tempdir(), "addpkg") dir.create(pkg) writeLines(   c(     "Package: addpkg",     "Title: Demo",     "Version: 0.1.0",     "Description: Demo.",     "License: MIT"   ),   file.path(pkg, "DESCRIPTION") ) use_jlbind(pkg) #> Created the binding package addpkgBindings in /tmp/RtmpP4r2qA/addpkg/inst/julia. #> Wrote /tmp/RtmpP4r2qA/addpkg/src/entrypoints.h (1 entrypoints).  # Add an entrypoint to the binding package, before its closing `end` file <- file.path(pkg, "inst/julia/src/addpkgBindings.jl") code <- readLines(file) last <- max(which(code == "end")) code <- append(   code,   c(     "add(x::Float64, y::Float64) = x + y",     "@rcall add(x::Float64, y::Float64)::Float64",     ""   ),   after = last - 1L ) writeLines(code, file)  update_entrypoints(pkg) #> Wrote /tmp/RtmpP4r2qA/addpkg/src/entrypoints.h (2 entrypoints). # The package now calls it as .Call(C_add, x, y)

title: Set up a package to use jlbind — use_jlbind
code: # A new package in a temporary directory pkg <- file.path(tempdir(), "mypkg") dir.create(pkg) writeLines(   c(     "Package: mypkg",     "Title: Demo",     "Version: 0.1.0",     "Description: Demo.",     "License: MIT"   ),   file.path(pkg, "DESCRIPTION") )  use_jlbind(pkg) #> Created the binding package mypkgBindings in /tmp/RtmpP4r2qA/mypkg/inst/julia. #> Wrote /tmp/RtmpP4r2qA/mypkg/src/entrypoints.h (1 entrypoints). list.files(pkg, recursive = TRUE) #> [1] "DESCRIPTION"                     "NAMESPACE"                       #> [3] "R/jlbind.R"                      "inst/julia/Project.toml"         #> [5] "inst/julia/src/mypkgBindings.jl" "src/entrypoints.h"               #> [7] "src/jlbind.c"                     # The Julia binding package, with its example entrypoint writeLines(readLines(file.path(pkg, "inst/julia/src/mypkgBindings.jl"))) #> """ #>     mypkgBindings #>  #> The R entrypoints of the R package mypkg. Each `@rcall` declaration #> exports a function R calls as `.Call(C_<name>, ...)`; after changing them, run #> `jlbind::update_entrypoints()` to regenerate `src/entrypoints.h`. #> """ #> module mypkgBindings #>  #> using JLBind #>  #> hello(name::String) = "Hello, " * name * ", from Julia!" #>  #> @rcall hello(name::String)::String #>  #> end
